01 / INTRODUCTION

Alan Tang

University of Virginia · History & Foreign Affairs

Hello! I’m Alan, a first-year student at the University of Virginia. My academic and professional interests center on military history, U.S. grand strategy, foreign policy, and the relationship between national security and economic power.

I study how the United States uses military, diplomatic, and economic tools in strategic competition, with a particular focus on U.S.–China relations.

04 / POLARITY GROUP

Polarity Group

Independent research initiative

I'm building a student-led research initiative focused on U.S.–China strategic competition. We examine where industrial capacity, strategic resources, and technology create consequential dependencies.

Rare-earth magnet intelligence +

Mapping the companies and facilities behind rare-earth permanent magnets, with attention to production status, supply chains, and alternatives to Chinese production.

Defense & industrial capacity +

Research interests include shipbuilding, munitions production, aerospace manufacturing, and industrial chokepoints.

Strategic resources & technology +

Connecting critical minerals and processing capacity to downstream components, technology dependencies, and the ability to scale production.

The goal: clear visual research that helps people understand where dependencies actually matter.
